newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends firmer after New York rally.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends firmer after New York rally.

text.p: London cocoa futures ended firmer on Tuesday as they tracked a rally in New York, but outright volume was relatively thin, traders said.
"New York led the way," said one trader.
A large volume of Dec/March switches was recorded in total turnover of 8,975 lots. Dec/March traded at 36-37 stg and March featured an AA deal of 1,500 lots, said to be by SFH.
The market found support after a brief decline in reaction to sterling's moves after the UK budget was announced.
Sterling was off its highs at $1.6725 after a bumpy ride during the announcement.
Benchmark March cocoa ended nine stg higher at 936 stg a tonne after a session high of 938. The low for the day was 924.
December saw extensive liquidation before its first tender day next week and gained nine stg to 900. Traders said the Dec/March monitor was also being used by some players to push prices higher.

Traders expected London to benefit from positive chart formations in New York, where the March contract has closed a previously elusive gap at $1,408 and moved above the technically difficult $1,410 on short covering.
"That will give us the impetus we needed," said one.
London's March will battle with resistance at 943.

Reaction to Ghana's cocoa purchases in the fourth week of the season was mild. Purchases totalled 19,308 tonnes by November 7 with the seasonal total reaching 94,500 tonnes, compared with 130,467 by November 9 last year.
"It has underpinned the market," a trader said.
In other news, the governor of Indonesia's key growing region of South Sulawesi ordered farmers to stop selling unfermented cocoa to improve the quality of traded beans.
